# Deckie

> Deckie is a booth companion for DJs who play on gear that does not know their music: turntables, older CDJs, a venue's own decks. Deckie Desk (Mac), on the DJ's computer, reads a crate, a group of the DJ's own songs, for tempo, key, bars and vocals, and writes a crate file with no audio in it. Deckie (the iPad app) sits beside the decks, listens, names the playing song from that crate, reads the pitch fader, and shows what could come next and how it could be brought in. A DJ with no iPad can switch Deckie Desk to Booth: it listens through the computer's microphone, names the song and shows the picks. The music never leaves the DJ's devices. Deckie is in development and has not been released; the site is a coming-soon page. Made by Christopher Shannon and App Hold Media (https://apphold.media).

Words used on the site, as the project defines them: a library is all the music a DJ owns; a crate is a group of songs and can be the whole library; a crate file is what Deckie Desk writes from a crate (tempo, key, bars, style and fingerprints, never audio) and what the iPad app carries. Deckie is the whole product and also the name of the iPad app (called Deckie Booth until November 2026); Deckie Desk is the Mac app, and Booth is its listening mode. The tagline is "Know Your Crate".

Status, stated exactly: Deckie Desk builds crate files on a Mac and Deckie runs on an iPad; it has been used for one night behind real decks and tested with a crate of 2,327 songs. There is no public beta yet and nothing in an app store; DJs who want to help test can write to info@apphold.media. Planned and not built: Deckie Desk for Windows and Linux (the shared Swift core already builds and passes its tests there), learning how a particular DJ mixes, and recognition across the whole range of the pitch fader. Deckie suggests and never instructs: it plays nothing, mixes nothing and does not touch the decks. It does not beatmatch. Nothing is uploaded, and what a DJ plays is not sent anywhere or used to train anything; there is no account, and it works with no signal.

## Pages

- [Home](https://deckie.io/): what Deckie does in the booth, what Deckie is not, how Deckie Desk prepares a crate file (with Desk's quick start, a short film, and its four steps in words), a short about with a list of facts, and a film with a written description of what it shows
- [Dictionary](https://deckie.io/dictionary/): DJ speak, in plain words. A dictionary for anyone, A to Z: each word in plain words, then how DJs use it, with a short note on what Deckie does with it
- [Privacy](https://deckie.io/privacy/): the privacy policy. No account, no analytics, no tracking; Deckie on the iPad does not use the internet; Deckie Desk on a Mac sends a song's names to MusicBrainz only when the DJ asks it to look them up.

## Optional

- [The film](https://deckie.io/assets/deckie-explainer.mp4): 76 seconds, words on screen, no voice; the home page has its content as text
- [Deckie Desk's quick start](https://deckie.io/assets/deckie-desk-quick-start.mp4): under a minute, no sound, words on screen: add music, Desk reads every song, the crate file to the iPad, Deckie beside the decks, and Booth in Desk for a DJ with no iPad; the home page has its four steps as text
- [The first fifteen seconds](https://deckie.io/assets/deckie-15s.mp4): the same film's opening, cut to stand alone
